Guillermo Rauch (CEO at Vercel) · 23h
We will all be learning in coming weeks & months, that most human-made software:

▪️ Was really slow
▪️ Had many security vulnerabilities
▪️ Was under-specified and incorrect

AI will rewrite it all. Many times. It will make it fast, cost-efficient, and secure. It will think about failure modes we couldn't wrap our heads around.

It will prove, formally verify, load test, harden. It will turn memory-unsafe foundations into robust, optimized ones. If you ask, it'll thoroughly document it, teach you about it, make diagrams, animations, and slide decks.

In many ways, we are witnessing the true birth of software engineering.

Trevor Spires (Applied AI @ Anthropic) · 1d • Edited
Big steps! I removed my code editor from my Dock today. Happy to reclaim that valuable real-estate from my desktop. 🖥️

No more IDE for me. I just kind of naturally stopped using the IDE/CLI. CLI/IDEs feel like a workbench, but these days writing code feels more like delegation than a collaborative act.

For collaboration I need a workbench, but for delegation I need more of a “command center”

My workflow is basically 1/ tell claude to do something 2/ have claude explain what it did 3/ have it draw a picture or write a doc about what it did if I need to understand the nuance. I stay in the Claude App or Slack mostly. Sometimes I open a chrome tab.

Nowhere in that flow is it useful for me to open up the code and read it. Claude is better at reading code than me anyways. And there's bigger fish to fry. 🐟
[Visit my website](https://www.youtube.com/@trevspires)
